notes: The pieces of the program's data by the file of assets/data that holds them, a file by subject: its description, then {piece name: format} (null: 16-bit words, or a fill when it is one byte over and over); tools/formats/ has the formats. A piece no file lists goes with the one before it.

system/system.description: the data of the main program: the attract mode, the controls, the interrupts, the coins and credits, the EEPROM settings and the bookkeeping, the sound requests

system/attract_demos.description: the attract mode's demos: the inputs they replay

system/test_mode.description: the test mode's screens: the menus and their texts, the CRT test patterns, the coin settings, the input, output, memory and sound tests, the backup clear

video/video.description: the video data the program shares: the text layer's fonts, the video registers' defaults, palette lists, VRAM scripts, the bitmap layer's tables

video/palettes.description: the palettes the program shares: the sprites', the tile banks', the text and bitmap layers' and the backdrop's, with their lists and repeat counts (each stage's own are in stages/)

video/sprite_frames.description: sprite_frame_records: every sprite frame's size and where its graphics are in the sprite ROM (assets/sprites holds the frames, in sheets)

engine/engine.description: the object system's data: the object types and kinds, spawn tables, contacts, projection and math tables, animation tables, the sprite palettes

objects/shared.description: the objects several stages use: rings, signs, scenery sprites, walls, the zones behind the chasers, the pacer, the hold on a group leader

objects/eggman.description: Eggman: his booth, his speech scripts, his scene with the button box

player/player.description: the players' data: starting, movement, states, effects and the HUD (positions, texts, gauges)

stages/shared.description: what the stage code and several stages share: the tables by stage (camera sections, scroll, palettes, layers, events, spawn lists), the tile sets, and the stages with almost nothing of their own (1, 2, 12)

stages/stage_00.description: stage 0, the tower top: its tilemaps, palettes and scenes

stages/intro.description: the scenes that start a game: stage 6's opening and stage 7's how to play, their objects and backgrounds

stages/stage_03.description: stage 3: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stage_04.description: stage 4: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stage_05.description: stage 5: its spawn lists, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stage_08.description: stage 8, the lava: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stage_09.description: stage 9, the ice: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stage_0a.description: stage A, the sand: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

stages/stages_0b_0f.description: stages B to F: their spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and their objects' data

stages/stage_10.description: stage 10, the river: its spawn lists, floor blocks, restart points, palettes and tilemaps, and its objects' data

scenes/title.description: the title screen: its pictures (tilemaps), palettes and animations

scenes/map.description: the map screen between stages: the island, the trails, the markers

scenes/character_select.description: choosing a character: the choosers' positions, portraits and texts

scenes/ranking.description: the ranking: the default table, the texts and letters, entering initials

scenes/ring_tally.description: the ring tally after a stage

scenes/ending.description: the ending (stage 0x11): the scenes, the flights and paths, the credits

system/code_read_as_data.description: the bytes of the program's code the game also reads as data (assets.json, read_as_data): the C replaces the code, and the game still reads these
